name: edit-row-diff-expands
opens_with: (/voice to clear the boot notice; the edit row comes from the agent script)
notes:
2026-11-03. The per-row half of click-to-expand, and the reason this scenario exists at all: a UNIT TEST CANNOT PROVE IT. operant_model/cache.rs:122 has `if cfg!(test) { return render(...) }` at the top of get_cached_message_lines, so every in-process test bypasses the row cache entirely. Mutating the cache key (row_expanded: false) and re-running render_tool_message_row_expansion_uncollapses_the_diff proves it: the test still PASSES. So the cache-key half of this feature is only observable in a real process, which is exactly what this scenario supplies.

The screen assertions are the load-bearing ones: `count:more changes==0` (the truncation row '... N more changes ...' is gone once the row is expanded) and `contains:let g = 77` (a line the truncated middle and dropped head both hid). The state assertion `expanded_tool_id == "e1"` pins that the click landed on the row rather than falling through to a text selection.

Row coordinate measured from a frame dump, not assumed. See the sibling tool-row-click-expands scenario for the method.
